title: Section 25 HMA — Permanent alimony and maintenance

content.overview: Section 25 allows the court, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, to order either party to pay the other a gross sum or monthly or periodical sum for maintenance and support, having regard to income, property, conduct, and other circumstances, with power to vary, modify, or rescind the order.
content.study: Permanent alimony is typically tied to a decree under the Act (nullity, restitution, judicial separation, or divorce). Conduct and remarriage can affect continuance. Distinguish interim support under section 24 from this lasting award. Read alongside sections 13 and 13B when advising on settlement packages at divorce.

learningObjectives: Explain Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 25 and its statutory purpose.
Identify and apply the provision's ingredients to a factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related HMA remedies.
enhancement.definition: Section 25 permits the court, at the time of passing a decree or subsequently, to order permanent alimony or maintenance in a gross sum or periodical payment, subject to the statutory factors and conditions.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Permanent alimony under Section 25 is discretionary and depends on the statutory circumstances, including income, property, conduct and other relevant factors; the order can be varied, modified or rescinded as provided by the section.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 25, including its provisions on modification/rescission and remarriage or other statutory consequences.
essentialIngredients: A decree under the Act or qualifying matrimonial proceeding must exist as required by Section 25.
Court considers income, property, conduct and circumstances of the parties.
Relief may be a gross sum or monthly/periodical sum.
The order remains subject to statutory variation, modification or rescission provisions.
Remarriage and other statutory conditions must be checked where relevant.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 25 provides continuing financial relief distinct from Section 24's interim maintenance. The Supreme Court has recently clarified that a spouse of a marriage declared void under Section 11 may invoke Section 25, but the grant remains discretionary and fact-dependent. The court also considers conduct and the statutory requirements when determining the relief.
examples: After a decree under the HMA, a spouse seeks permanent alimony. The court examines the parties' income, property, conduct and other circumstances and may order a lump sum or periodic payment, subject to the statutory framework.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 25 is permanent alimony/maintenance linked to the statutory matrimonial decree framework; Section 24 is interim maintenance during proceedings.

caseLaw.name: Sukhdev Singh v. Sukhbir Kaur
caseLaw.citation: Civil Appeal Nos. 2536 and 5726 of 2019; order dated 4 June 2026
caseLaw.holding: Order dated 4 June 2026. The Court recorded that a spouse whose marriage has been declared void under Section 11 is entitled to seek permanent alimony or maintenance under Section 25, but whether that relief is granted depends on the facts of the case and the conduct of the parties, and the grant is always discretionary. It set aside the impugned orders insofar as they dealt with interim alimony under Section 24 and permanent alimony under Section 25, and remitted those issues for evidence, leaving the Section 11 decree undisturbed.
caseLaw.relevance: Opened order on the availability of Section 25 permanent alimony after a decree declaring the marriage void under Section 11.

caseLaw.name: Amutha v. A.R. Subramanian
caseLaw.holding: Judgment dated 19 December 2024. While upholding the divorce decree, the Court directed the husband to pay Rs 50,00,000 as permanent alimony to the wife and a further Rs 50,00,000 to the daughter, within four months. It treated financial independence as not precluding such relief where needed to secure dignity and stability, and it recorded factors drawn from Rajnesh v. Neha, including duration of the marriage, earning capacities, age and health, standard of living, and contributions to the marriage.
caseLaw.relevance: Opened judgment that awarded permanent alimony while upholding a divorce decree.

enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the decree, assess statutory eligibility, collect financial and conduct evidence, determine the appropriate form of award, and check grounds for later variation or rescission.
